title: The Boerne, Texas Real Estate Market
metaTitle: Boerne TX Real Estate Market: Prices, Inventory and What Actually Drives Value
metaDescription: Boerne TX real estate: median sale price, inventory, tax rates and the city-limits line that moves a tax bill by $2,800 a year. Local agent analysis.
summary: Boerne's median sale price is about $602,600, up 3.0% year over year, with 308 active listings against 832 trailing-twelve-month closings — roughly 4.4 months of inventory (SABOR MLS, September 2026). The biggest value driver is jurisdiction: inside city limits the combined 2025 tax rate is 1.8645 versus 1.3929 unincorporated, about $2,840 a year.
body:
Most market reports about Boerne are wrong before the first paragraph ends, because they treat "Boerne" as one place. It isn't. A Boerne mailing address can put you inside a city with its own electric utility, a dark-sky lighting code and a 1.86 combined tax rate — or seven miles up a county road with a well, a septic system, no zoning of any kind, and a 1.39 rate. Same school district. Same zip. A difference of roughly $2,800 a year in property tax on a median-priced house.

That distinction is the single most important thing to understand about this market, and it drives almost everything below.

Where the market sits right now

As of September 2026, per SABOR MLS:

Metric Figure
Active listings 308
Closed sales, trailing 12 months 832
Median sale price ~$602,600
Year-over-year appreciation +3.0%

Run the absorption math and you get roughly 69 sales a month against 308 actives — about 4.4 months of inventory. That is a market that has stopped being a seller's market without becoming a buyer's market. Six months is the traditional balance point; under three months sellers dictate terms. At 4.4 months, Boerne is in the zone where a correctly priced, well-prepared house still sells in a normal window and an overpriced one sits until it gets stale and takes a discount.

The +3.0% year-over-year number is the one people misread. After the 2020-2022 run, 3% feels like a stall. It isn't a stall — it is the market reverting to something close to its long-run behavior. What it does mean is that appreciation is no longer covering your cost of sale. At a 6% total cost to sell, a 3% annual gain means a two-year hold is roughly break-even. Short holds don't work here right now. Plan on five years or don't buy.

Why the median is $602,600 and what that number hides

A median above $600,000 in a Texas town of about 24,000 people surprises out-of-state buyers. Two things explain it.

First, the land. Kendall County's 2025 certified appraisal roll shows $1.98 billion in agricultural market value inside Boerne ISD alone, appraised at just $9.2 million under productivity valuation — a $1.97 billion productivity loss (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals, as of Supplement 47, December 3, 2025). That is a county where a very large share of the ground is still ranch land carrying an ag valuation. Ranch land converts to residential acreage slowly, and every conversion prices off Hill Country land comps, not subdivision comps.

Second, the mix. Boerne ISD covers 24,924 taxable property accounts with a total market value of $14.74 billion. The City of Boerne accounts for only 9,157 of those accounts. Roughly two-thirds of the taxable property in this school district sits outside city limits (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals). Acreage properties, custom builds on one to ten acres, and gated ranch developments pull the median up in a way a purely municipal market never would.

So "the Boerne market" is really three markets stacked on top of each other: in-town historic and infill, production and semi-custom subdivisions in the growth corridor along I-10, and acreage. They move at different speeds and they do not comp against each other. If somebody hands you a single price-per-square-foot number for Boerne, they are averaging a 1920s cottage on Main Street with a 2,000-foot ranch house on twelve acres. That number is noise.

The growth driver: people, not speculation

Kendall County's population was estimated at 53,289 in 2025, up 20.3% from 2020 (Community Impact, March 30, 2026, citing Census Bureau estimates). The City of Boerne was estimated at 24,047 as of July 2025. The county consistently ranks among the fastest-growing in Texas by percentage, and the dominant component is domestic in-migration — people moving here, not births.

Domestic in-migration is a more durable demand source than investor speculation, and it behaves differently. It is less rate-sensitive at the margin because the buyer is moving for a reason that isn't financial — a job, a school district, a parent, a retirement plan. It also means your competition as a seller is not just the other listings; it is the buyer's alternative of renting for a year while they figure the area out.

What actually drives value in Boerne

1. Boerne ISD

Boerne ISD earned an A rating with an overall score of 92 in the Texas Education Agency accountability ratings released in August 2026, covering the 2025-26 school year — the district's seventh consecutive A. Domain scores were 93 in Student Achievement, 83 in School Progress and 90 in Closing the Gaps, with a 99.2% graduation rate (Boerne Star, August 19, 2026).

That rating is the demand engine. It is why a family in a good Bexar County district will still pay a premium to cross the county line. It is also why the western and northern parts of Kendall County — which are served by Comfort ISD, not Boerne ISD — price differently. Comfort ISD's 2025 adopted rate was $0.9328 versus Boerne ISD's $1.0109 (Kendall Appraisal District), so the tax is lower, but the school-driven demand premium is not there in the same way. Buyers conflate "Boerne address" with "Boerne ISD" constantly. Verify the district before you write an offer.

2. The city-limits line

Adopted rates for tax year 2025, per Kendall Appraisal District:

Entity Rate per $100
Boerne ISD 1.0109
City of Boerne 0.4716
Kendall County 0.3770
Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District 0.0050

Combined, a house inside Boerne city limits in Boerne ISD pays 1.8645. The same house in unincorporated Kendall County in Boerne ISD pays 1.3929. On the $602,600 median, that difference is $2,841.86 a year — about $237 a month of escrow, before you touch the loan.

You do not get that for free. Outside the city you are on a well or a shared water system and a septic system, you have no municipal electric or gas, and you have no city inspection backing the house. Inside the city you get Boerne Utilities — the city operates its own electric, natural gas, water, wastewater, stormwater and reclaimed water systems — plus trash, plus a building department. That is a real trade, not a loophole.

3. Municipal utility districts

Two MUDs sit inside Kendall County and they are not small additions. Kendall County MUD #1 adds 0.65 to the rate; Miralomas MUD adds 1.00 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025). A house in Miralomas MUD carries a combined 2.3929 rate — on a $602,600 home with a homestead exemption that is roughly $13,000 a year in property tax versus about $6,978 for the same house in unincorporated Kendall County with no MUD.

MUD disclosure is required in Texas, and it is delivered — but buyers routinely sign it without doing the math. Do the math. A 1.00 MUD rate on a $700,000 house is $7,000 a year, which is roughly $1,100 a month of purchasing power at current rates.

4. Water

Kendall County sits in the Hill Country Priority Groundwater Management Area, and the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District was created by county voters in November 2002 to manage the Trinity Aquifer (Cow Creek GCD). Outside the city, water is a diligence item on par with the foundation. Well depth, yield, recent drought performance, whether the well is registered, and what the district's drought stage rules do to permitted users are all real questions with real answers. On acreage, "there's a well" is not a finding. Get the yield test.

5. No county zoning

The Kendall County Engineer's office states plainly that the county "does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas of the County," and that the county "has not adopted building codes for single family residential developments" (Kendall County Engineer verification letter, March 4, 2026). The county does permit driveways, work in county right-of-way, outdoor lighting, on-site sewage facilities, floodplain development and site improvements, and it has adopted a Fire Code administered by the Fire Marshal.

Two consequences. One, your protection against what gets built next door is the subdivision's deed restrictions and HOA — nothing else. Read them before you buy, and read them for what they don't prohibit. Two, a house built outside the city was not inspected by a municipal building department. Your third-party inspection is doing all of the work. Do not waive it on a country property. Ever.

Where I think this market goes

I won't forecast prices. Anyone who does is guessing. But three things are structurally true and worth planning around.

Supply is constrained by more than builder appetite. Septic feasibility, well yield, floodplain along Cibolo Creek and its tributaries, and the sheer cost of extending city utilities all cap how fast lots come online. That is a different constraint than a flat metro market with land in every direction.

Demand is driven by in-migration and a school rating, both of which are slow-moving. Neither turns off in a quarter.

And the tax picture is not static. Boerne ISD passed a voter-approval tax rate election on November 4, 2025, canvassed November 18, generating about $4.8 million — $3 million local, $1.8 million state — with more than 80% going to compensation, including raising the teacher minimum starting salary from $55,142 to $60,000 (Community Impact, November 18, 2025). A fast-growth district with rising enrollment will keep coming back to voters. Underwrite your tax escrow with that in mind rather than assuming today's rate is permanent.

Read next

  • Buying a Home in Boerne, TX — the process, timeline, and what's different from a San Antonio purchase
  • Boerne Property Taxes Explained — every rate, every exemption, the actual math
  • Boerne vs. San Antonio — the honest comparison, including the cases where San Antonio wins

Working through a Boerne move? Send me the address you're looking at and I'll tell you the school zone, the exact combined tax rate for that parcel, whether it's in a MUD, and whether it's city water or a well — before you spend a Saturday driving out. That's a ten-minute answer for me and a week of guessing for you.

title: Buying a Home in Boerne, TX
metaTitle: Buying a Home in Boerne, TX: Process, Timeline and Local Traps
metaDescription: How buying in Boerne differs from San Antonio: wells, septic, no county zoning, MUD rates, and the diligence that actually matters. From a local agent.
summary: The contract mechanics match any Texas purchase; the diligence does not. Before touring, verify four things: city limits or unincorporated (1.8645 versus 1.3929 combined 2025 rate), MUD status, Boerne ISD versus Comfort ISD, and the deed restrictions. Kendall County has no zoning and no residential building code, so well, septic and inspection carry the whole load.
body:
The mechanics of a Texas purchase are the same in Boerne as anywhere else in the state: TREC contract, option period, third-party financing addendum, title commitment, survey, closing at a title company. If you've bought in Texas before, none of that will surprise you.

What's different is the diligence. In San Antonio, the systems question is "does the AC work." In Kendall County, outside the city, the systems question includes "where does the water come from, where does the sewage go, and who inspected any of this." That is where Boerne purchases go wrong, and it is almost always a diligence failure rather than a negotiation failure.

Step one, before you tour anything: figure out which Boerne you're buying

Do this before you fall in love with a listing. There are four questions and they change the price of ownership by thousands a year.

1. Is it inside Boerne city limits? Inside, the combined 2025 tax rate for a Boerne ISD property is 1.8645 per $100. Outside, in unincorporated Kendall County, it's 1.3929 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 adopted rates). On a $600,000 house that is about $2,830 a year. Inside the city you also get Boerne Utilities — city electric, natural gas, water, wastewater, stormwater and reclaimed water — and a building department. Outside you get well, septic, and an electric cooperative.

2. Is it in a MUD? Kendall County MUD #1 adds 0.65 to the rate. Miralomas MUD adds 1.00. That is not a rounding error — a 1.00 MUD rate on a $700,000 home is $7,000 a year. Texas requires MUD notice, and you will get it, but get it early enough to matter rather than on the day you sign.

3. Is it Boerne ISD or Comfort ISD? A Boerne mailing address does not guarantee Boerne ISD. The western and northern reaches of Kendall County are Comfort ISD. Boerne ISD's own guidance is that "homes located near the school district boundary lines must be verified by the Administrative Services Department" — the district's InfoFinder tool plus a phone call to Administrative Services at (830) 357-2011 is the only answer I trust. Not the listing. Not Zillow. Not the seller.

4. Is there an HOA, and what do its restrictions actually say? This matters more in Kendall County than it does in a city, because outside the municipal limits the deed restrictions are the only land-use control. Kendall County's own County Engineer states the county "does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas" (Kendall County Engineer verification letter, March 4, 2026). If the restrictions don't prohibit it, it can be built next to you.

The country-property diligence list

This is the part that separates a Boerne buyer's agent from someone who works the whole metro and lands here twice a year.

Water

If it's a well, you need three things: a yield test, a bacteriological and chemical water test, and the well's registration status with the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District. Kendall County sits inside the Hill Country Priority Groundwater Management Area, and Cow Creek GCD was created by county voters in 2002 specifically to manage Trinity Aquifer withdrawal.

The failure mode is a well that produces fine in March and struggles in August. Ask the seller for their pump records and ask the neighbors what happened in the last drought — neighbors are a better data source than any document on this particular question. If it's a shared well, the shared-well agreement needs to be read line by line: who pays for the pump, what happens when it fails, and what the remedy is if the other party won't pay.

If it's a water supply corporation or a WCID, get the connection fee and the monthly rate in writing before the option period ends.

Septic (OSSF)

Kendall County permits on-site sewage facilities, and the county's permitting authority approves or denies an application within 30 days of receipt (Kendall County). For an existing system, you want the permit on file, the design, the last pump-out record, and a dedicated septic inspection — not the general home inspector's five-minute look. Aerobic systems have maintenance contracts that transfer or lapse at closing; find out which.

For vacant land, the entire deal hinges on whether a system can be permitted at all. Soil, slope and setbacks decide that, and the answer requires a licensed site evaluator. Make the contract contingent on it.

The house itself

Kendall County "has not adopted building codes for single family residential developments" (County Engineer, March 2026). The county has adopted a Fire Code, administered by the Fire Marshal, and issues Certificates of Compliance and Occupancy for certain multi-family and non-residential development — but a single-family house built outside the city was not inspected by a municipal building department.

Your third-party inspection is the entire quality-control system on that house. Use a good inspector, be present, and budget for specialists: foundation, roof, septic, well, and — on older Hill Country homes — a look at the electrical service if there's any knob-and-tube or an early Federal Pacific panel.

Floodplain and drainage

Cibolo Creek and its tributaries have produced significant flooding in the Boerne area repeatedly. Flood zone designation varies parcel by parcel, sometimes within the same subdivision, and the FEMA FIRM panel for the exact parcel is the only reliable source. Texas seller's disclosure requires disclosure of known flooding and certain floodplain status, and I read that section carefully on every Boerne contract.

Two additional notes. FEMA maps do not capture every risk in Central Texas — flash flooding happens outside mapped zones routinely. And on acreage, ask where the low-water crossing is between the house and the highway. A property that is dry but unreachable eight times a year is a real problem that no map will tell you about.

Access and easements

On rural tracts, confirm legal access, not just a gravel road that has always been there. The survey and the title commitment's Schedule B are where this lives. Pipeline easements, utility easements and shared driveway arrangements all show up here. Order a new survey — an old one that predates a fence line, a pond or an outbuilding will cost you more in a title fight than the survey saved.

Outdoor lighting

Kendall County requires a permit prior to installing any outdoor lights, and regulated outdoor lighting must use International Dark-Sky Association compliant products. The City of Boerne has its own dark-sky regulations in its Unified Development Code. If you're planning arena lights, a lit sport court or extensive landscape lighting, check before you budget for it.

Timeline

A typical financed Boerne purchase runs 30 to 45 days from executed contract to funding. The pieces:

  • Option period: negotiated, commonly 7 to 10 days. On a country property I push for longer, because you are stacking a general inspection, a septic inspection, a well test and sometimes a structural engineer inside that window, and rural inspectors book out further than city ones.
  • Earnest money and option fee: delivered per the contract's timelines. Texas contract deadlines are strict and the clock does not care about weekends or holidays.
  • Survey: order it the day the option period starts, not the day before closing. Rural surveys take longer.
  • Appraisal: acreage and custom homes appraise slower and with more variance, because the comparable set is thin. An appraiser working from a San Antonio comp pool will get an acreage property wrong. Ask your lender to order a local appraiser.
  • Title: Schedule B review is a real step here, not a formality.

One timing note that costs people money: if your contract executes on a Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, your option period is running while the title company is closed for part of it. Under a short option, that can leave you delivering an option fee or terminating on a day when nobody is available to help. Push execution to earlier in the week when you can, or negotiate a longer option.

Financing considerations specific to this market

Acreage and the appraisal. Many conventional products limit how much of a property's value can be in land versus improvements, and outbuildings, barns and arenas often contribute far less to appraised value than they cost to build. If you're buying a property where half the value is a shop and twelve acres, talk to a lender who does rural lending in this county before you write.

Ag valuation. If the land you're buying carries a 1-d-1 open-space agricultural valuation and you don't continue a qualifying use, you can trigger a rollback. The Kendall Appraisal District's ag guidelines are specific — cow/calf requires a minimum of three calves on ten acres, beekeeping requires not less than five nor more than twenty acres with a minimum of six hives, wildlife management requires a minimum of three approved practices, and the land must have been in qualifying ag use for five of the preceding seven years (Kendall County Ag Use Manual). Decide before closing whether you intend to maintain the valuation.

Homestead exemption. File it. Texas Tax Code 11.13(b) requires school districts to provide a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and Kendall Appraisal District's adopted exemption schedule shows that $140,000 applied at Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD. Note carefully: neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general residence homestead exemption (Kendall Appraisal District adopted rates and exemptions). Kendall County offers $10,000 for over-65 and disabled persons; the City of Boerne offers a freeze for qualifying over-65 and disabled homesteads but no general homestead percentage. So the full value of your homestead exemption here is the school-district piece — roughly $1,415 a year at the 2025 Boerne ISD rate.

Also worth knowing: a buyer who acquires property after January 1 may receive the residence homestead exemption for the applicable portion of that tax year immediately upon qualifying, if the prior owner did not already have it for that year (Kendall Appraisal District, Updated Property Tax Information, March 2026).

Short-term rentals — do not import San Antonio's rules

If you're buying with any intent to short-term rent, the City of San Antonio's STR ordinance does not apply in Boerne. Boerne is in Kendall County and is its own municipality with its own rules.

Under the City of Boerne's short-term rental ordinance, an STR operating inside city limits or in the city's extraterritorial jurisdiction must be registered and permitted by the City. The permit fee is $200, permits expire two years from the effective date with a $200 renewal, and properties inside city limits require a safety inspection at a cost of $100 (ETJ properties are exempt from the inspection requirement). In residentially zoned areas, an STR cannot operate within 200 feet of another STR on the same block face. Owners must carry minimum liability coverage of $500,000 per occurrence and $1 million in the aggregate, occupancy is limited to two people per bedroom plus two additional, and hotel occupancy taxes must be remitted. The City's Planning Department is at (830) 248-1501.

For property in unincorporated Kendall County outside any city's ETJ, verify the rules directly with Kendall County and the City of Boerne before you underwrite an STR. I am not going to tell you it's unregulated based on the absence of an ordinance I found online. Call and get it in writing.

Before you drive out to a showing, send me the address. I'll come back with the school zone verified with the district, the exact combined tax rate for that parcel, MUD status, whether it's city water or a well, and the FEMA zone. That's the difference between a productive Saturday and a wasted one.

title: Selling a Home in Boerne, TX
metaTitle: Selling a Home in Boerne, TX: Pricing, Prep, Timeline and Net Proceeds
metaDescription: Selling in Boerne at 4.4 months of inventory: how to price acreage with thin comps, what prep pays, and how to read your net sheet. Local agent guide.
summary: At roughly 4.4 months of inventory and 3.0% annual appreciation (SABOR MLS, September 2026), appreciation no longer rescues a pricing mistake — price correctly in week one. Comps are thin because in-town, subdivision and acreage Boerne do not cross-comp. Documentation of well, septic and ag records removes the buyer's uncertainty discount cheaply.
body:
Boerne is at roughly 4.4 months of inventory — 308 active listings against 832 closings over the trailing twelve months, or about 69 sales a month (as of September 2026, per SABOR MLS). Median sale price is about $602,600, up 3.0% year over year.

That combination defines the job. Four and a half months of supply is a market where a correctly priced house sells on a normal timeline and an overpriced one does not sell at all until it takes a visible price cut. And 3% annual appreciation means the market will not bail out a pricing mistake. In 2021 you could list 8% high and let appreciation catch up to you in five months. That is over.

Pricing: the part that's genuinely hard here

In a tract subdivision with 400 identical floor plans, pricing is arithmetic. In Boerne, on the properties where the money is, it is judgment — and the most common failure I see is an agent running a one-mile radius search and calling it a CMA.

Why Boerne comps are thin

Three separate markets sit inside the same MLS area and they don't cross-comp:

In-town Boerne. Historic district, older infill, walkable to Main Street. Lot value is a large share of total value and condition varies enormously house to house. This is the segment where a bad renovation and a great renovation can sit on the same block with the same square footage and a $150,000 spread.

Subdivision Boerne. Production and semi-custom neighborhoods in the growth corridor. This is the closest thing to a normal comp environment, and even here the difference between a 2016 build and a 2024 build in the same subdivision is a real adjustment, not a rounding error.

Acreage. Kendall Appraisal District's 2025 certified roll shows $1.98 billion of agricultural market value inside Boerne ISD alone, appraised at $9.2 million under productivity valuation. That is a county where a great deal of the ground is still ranch. When acreage sells, it prices off land comps plus improvement contribution — and improvements on acreage routinely contribute far less than they cost to build.

If your property is acreage, an honest CMA may only have four or five genuinely comparable sales and some of them will be six or twelve months old. That is fine. What is not fine is an agent pretending otherwise and adjusting a subdivision sale up to fit.

The adjustments that actually move the number in this market

  • Land quality, not just acreage. Usable, fenced, cleared pasture is worth more per acre than cedar-choked slope. Frontage on a county-maintained road versus a shared gravel easement is a material difference. A live creek or a good stock tank is a premium; a dry drainage that floods is a discount.
  • Water. A strong, tested, registered well with documented yield is an asset you can put a number on. A well with no records is a discount, because the first buyer's inspection will find whatever is there anyway. Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District governs groundwater in Kendall County, and buyers are increasingly sophisticated about drought-stage rules.
  • Septic condition and capacity. A permitted, documented, recently serviced system with capacity matching the bedroom count closes without drama. An undocumented system is a negotiation the buyer will win.
  • School district. Boerne ISD versus Comfort ISD is a demand difference, and buyers verify it now. If you're on a boundary, get the district's written confirmation before you list so your marketing is accurate and defensible.
  • Tax rate. In city limits, 1.8645 combined. Unincorporated Boerne ISD, 1.3929. In Kendall County MUD #1, 2.0429. In Miralomas MUD, 2.3929 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 adopted rates). Your buyer's lender is qualifying them on that number. A house in a high-MUD district competes against a lower-rate house for a smaller buyer pool at the same price, and pricing has to respect that.

What your appraisal district value is not

Your Kendall Appraisal District notice is not a market value opinion you can list against. The district's 2025 roll for Boerne ISD shows $14.74 billion in market value against $8.93 billion in net taxable value — a gap created by ag productivity valuation ($1.97 billion), exemptions ($3.24 billion), the 10% homestead appraisal cap ($543 million) and the non-homestead circuit-breaker cap ($68.6 million). If you've owned a while and been protected by the 10% homestead cap, your assessed value may be well below market. If you protested successfully last year, it's lower still. Neither number tells a buyer what your house is worth.

Prep: what pays and what doesn't

I'll be blunt about this because sellers spend money in the wrong places.

Pays reliably:

  • Paint, in a neutral. It's the highest-return dollar in the business and it always has been.
  • Landscape cleanup and, on acreage, brush clearing along the approach and around the house. The drive in is the first impression and on a rural property it's 90 seconds long.
  • Deep clean and declutter. Not staging-magazine empty — just clean.
  • Fixing the obvious deferred item the buyer would otherwise use as a lever: the failed water heater, the visibly rotted trim, the fence section on the ground.
  • Documentation. This is underrated and nearly free. Well records, water test, septic permit and last pump-out, HVAC service history, roof age and any warranty, survey, HOA documents, and — if the land carries an ag valuation — the current ag records. A binder of documents removes the buyer's uncertainty discount. On a country property this is worth more than a new backsplash.

Usually doesn't pay:

  • Full kitchen remodels immediately before listing. You rarely recover the cost and you're guessing at someone else's taste.
  • High-end fixtures in a mid-market house.
  • Pools, obviously, but also: outbuildings, shops and arenas built right before sale. They will not appraise at cost.

The judgment call: a pre-listing inspection. In a 4.4-month market I usually recommend it on properties over about $700,000 and on anything rural. It costs a few hundred dollars and it converts a surprise during the option period — where the buyer holds all the leverage — into a known item you priced for. The downside is real: in Texas, once you know about a defect you must disclose it. Which means a pre-listing inspection is a commitment to fix or disclose, not a way to find out quietly. I'd rather you make that commitment on purpose than find out in week three.

Disclosure obligations that bite in Kendall County

The Texas seller's disclosure notice is a legal document and Boerne properties have more boxes that matter than a city house does.

  • Flooding. Known flooding, floodplain status, and prior claims. Cibolo Creek and its tributaries have flooded the Boerne area repeatedly. Disclose it.
  • Septic. Type, age, permit status, known issues.
  • Water. Well, shared well, water supply corporation, MUD, WCID. Shared-well agreements and their terms.
  • Easements and encroachments. Pipeline, utility, access.
  • HOA and deed restrictions. Including any active violation.
  • Structural repairs and previous inspections. Including that pre-listing inspection if you got one.

Because Kendall County has not adopted building codes for single-family residential construction in unincorporated areas (Kendall County Engineer verification letter, March 4, 2026), buyers here lean harder on disclosure and inspection than they would inside a city. An incomplete disclosure is the single most common route from "under contract" to "lawsuit" in this county.

Timeline

Working backward from a target closing date:

  • 2 to 4 weeks before listing: prep work, documentation gathering, photography scheduling. On acreage, add drone and boundary-overlay imagery — buyers cannot understand a 15-acre tract from ground-level photos.
  • Listing to contract: in a 4.4-month market, a correctly priced house in a desirable segment typically sees its serious activity in the first two to three weeks. If you've had ten showings and no offer, that's a price signal, not a marketing problem. If you've had two showings in three weeks, that's a price signal too — it means buyers are screening you out before they ever get in the car.
  • Contract to close: 30 to 45 days financed. Acreage and custom homes appraise slower, and a thin comp set means more appraisal risk. Build that into your expectations.

Net proceeds: read the whole sheet

A seller net sheet has more lines than most sellers expect. The ones people forget:

  • Commission, per your listing agreement.
  • Title policy. In this part of Texas the seller customarily pays the owner's title policy, but it is negotiable and it is negotiated.
  • Escrow, recording, and title company fees.
  • Survey, if you're providing one.
  • Prorated property taxes from January 1 through closing. On a $602,600 house in Boerne city limits with a homestead exemption, the full-year bill is roughly $9,820 — a June closing means you're bringing about half of that to the table. This is the number that surprises sellers most.
  • HOA transfer and resale certificate fees.
  • Payoff, including per-diem interest through the funding date, not the contract date.
  • Repair credits or buyer concessions negotiated during the option period.
  • Ag rollback exposure, if the land carries a 1-d-1 open-space valuation and the use is changing. This can be substantial and it is worth understanding before you list, not after.

Ask for your net sheet at two or three price points, and ask for it again the day you get an offer. A $15,000 price difference and a $10,000 concession are not the same thing on your bottom line, and they're not the same thing on the buyer's loan either.

The one thing I'd tell every Boerne seller

Price it right in week one. In a 3%-appreciation market with four and a half months of supply, the price you list at is the price that determines whether you get a first-week showing surge or a slow bleed. Every week a listing sits, the market reads it as a problem, and the eventual sale price after two reductions is almost always lower than the number you would have gotten by starting correctly.

title: Boerne vs. San Antonio: Which Should You Buy In?
metaTitle: Boerne vs. San Antonio: Which Should You Buy In?
metaDescription: Boerne or San Antonio? Verified 2025 tax rates side by side, schools, commute and the cases where San Antonio is the better buy. Honest local comparison.
summary: On an identical $602,600 house with a homestead exemption and 2025 adopted rates, annual property tax runs $6,978 in unincorporated Kendall County, $9,820 inside Boerne city limits, and $11,032 inside San Antonio in Northside ISD. Boerne's sticker prices are higher, but its effective rate is lower. Under about $450,000, San Antonio has the inventory.
body:
The conventional wisdom is that Boerne is the expensive option and San Antonio is the affordable one. On sticker price, that's true — Boerne's median sale price is about $602,600 (as of September 2026, per SABOR MLS), well above the San Antonio metro median.

On the rate you pay to own, the conventional wisdom is backwards. Let me show you, with the actual adopted numbers.

Property taxes: the comparison nobody runs correctly

Most "Boerne is cheaper" and "Boerne is more expensive" claims compare tax rates without accounting for exemptions. That's useless, because Bexar County entities offer generous local homestead exemptions and Kendall County entities largely do not. You have to run the math both ways.

The rates

Kendall County (tax year 2025, per Kendall Appraisal District):

Entity Rate Homestead exemption offered
Boerne ISD 1.0109 $140,000 (state-mandated); $60,000 additional for 65+/disabled
City of Boerne 0.4716 None (freeze available for qualifying 65+/disabled)
Kendall County 0.3770 None general; $10,000 for 65+/disabled
Cow Creek GCD 0.0050 None
Combined, in Boerne city limits 1.8645
Combined, unincorporated Kendall County 1.3929

Bexar County (tax year 2025, per Bexar County official rates):

Entity Rate Homestead exemption offered
Northside ISD 1.004900 $140,000 (state-mandated)
City of San Antonio 0.541590 $5,000 or 20%
Bexar County 0.276331 $5,000 or 20%
Hospital District (University Health) 0.276235 $5,000 or 20%
Alamo Community College District 0.149150 $5,000 or 1%
Bexar County Road and Flood Control 0.023668 $3,000 and 20%
San Antonio River Authority 0.018300 $5,000 or 4%
Combined 2.290174

Six county-wide entities stack in Bexar County before you even reach the school district. Kendall County has effectively two, plus a groundwater district that rounds to nothing.

The math on an identical $602,600 house

Same price, homestead exemption filed, 2025 adopted rates:

Location Annual property tax Effective rate
Unincorporated Kendall County, Boerne ISD $6,978 1.16%
Inside Boerne city limits, Boerne ISD $9,820 1.63%
Inside San Antonio city limits, Northside ISD $11,032 1.83%

Assumptions: $602,600 assessed value, general residence homestead only (no over-65, disability or veteran exemption), 2025 adopted rates as published by Kendall Appraisal District and Bexar County. A Bexar County property in Alamo Heights ISD or San Antonio ISD, or in unincorporated Bexar County, produces a different number. Your actual bill depends on your parcel.

So on the same purchase price, Boerne inside the city limits runs about $1,200 a year cheaper than San Antonio, and unincorporated Kendall County runs about $4,050 a year cheaper — roughly $338 a month of mortgage payment.

That is real and it surprises people. It survives even though San Antonio and Bexar County each give a 20% local homestead exemption that Boerne and Kendall County do not, because San Antonio simply has more entities taxing the same dirt.

The honest caveat

This compares the same price point, and that is not how most people actually shop. If your budget is $400,000, San Antonio has hundreds of options and Boerne has very few. The Boerne buyer is usually spending more in absolute dollars even though the rate is lower — they are buying a larger or newer house on more land, and the lower rate applied to a higher value can still produce a bigger check.

Run the comparison on the two houses you would actually buy, not on a hypothetical identical one.

The in-between case: Fair Oaks Ranch

There is a third option people miss. The City of Fair Oaks Ranch spans three counties — Kendall, Comal and Bexar — and property there is appraised by Kendall Appraisal District, Comal Appraisal District or Bexar Appraisal District depending on which side of the line your parcel falls on. The city is served by Boerne ISD and, for Comal County residents, Comal ISD. City property taxes are billed by the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector regardless of which county you live in (City of Fair Oaks Ranch).

The City of Fair Oaks Ranch's adopted 2025 rate is 0.285300 with a $5,000-or-percentage homestead exemption and a $50,000 over-65 exemption (Bexar County 2025 Official Tax Rates). That's a materially lower city rate than either Boerne (0.4716, no homestead exemption) or San Antonio (0.541590).

This is the single most error-prone address in the region. Two houses on the same Fair Oaks Ranch street can sit in different counties, be appraised by different appraisal districts, and land in different school districts. Do not assume. Pull the parcel.

Schools

Boerne ISD earned an A rating with an overall score of 92 in the TEA accountability ratings released in August 2026, covering the 2025-26 school year — the district's seventh consecutive A, with a 99.2% graduation rate (Boerne Star, August 19, 2026).

That's the cleanest single-variable advantage Boerne has. Bexar County contains excellent schools — Alamo Heights ISD, parts of Northside and North East ISD all perform strongly — but it also contains some of the state's weakest, and the distribution matters. In Bexar County you buy into a specific attendance zone and you monitor it, because zones get redrawn and campus performance varies within a district. In Boerne ISD, you're buying into a district that has rated A district-wide for seven straight years.

Two caveats a good agent gives you anyway:

Not every Boerne address is Boerne ISD. Western and northern Kendall County is Comfort ISD. Verify with the district, not the listing.

Boerne ISD is a fast-growth district and boundaries move. The board approved new elementary attendance boundaries in April 2024, creating a zone for Viola Wilson Elementary and relieving enrollment at Fabra, Kendall and Van Raub. If you're buying specifically for a campus, understand that the campus assignment is not permanent.

Commute

The corridor is I-10, and it's the whole conversation.

If you work in the northwest quadrant — the Medical Center, La Cantera, the UTSA area, the 1604/I-10 employment corridor — the Boerne commute is manageable and thousands of people do it daily. If you work downtown, on the South Side, or east of US 281, you are adding meaningful time in both directions and you should drive it at 7:15 a.m. on a Tuesday before you commit to it. Not on a Sunday afternoon. A Tuesday.

The chokepoint has historically been where Kendall County traffic meets Bexar County volume approaching Loop 1604. TxDOT has worked this corridor in stages, with a series of projects between Loop 1604 and SH 46 improving intersections, adding and widening overpasses, converting frontage roads to one-way operation and expanding main lanes. A further project covering I-10 from SH 46 to Fair Oaks Parkway in Kendall County has been studied at a proposed cost of $100 million (TxDOT, San Antonio District). Construction on a corridor like this is a decade-long condition, not an event — factor it in.

The upside nobody mentions: the commute is directional. Boerne to San Antonio in the morning and back in the evening runs with the flow, which is different from a suburb where you're fighting everyone.

Cost of living beyond the tax bill

Utilities. Inside Boerne city limits, the City owns and operates six utilities — electric, natural gas, water, wastewater, stormwater and reclaimed water. That means one provider, one bill, and rates set by City Council rather than by a competitive retail market. In February 2025 the average residential water and wastewater bill went from $90.46 to $94.71 per month, and the city has signaled further increases over a five-year horizon to fund its capital improvement plan (Community Impact, February 3, 2025). Outside city limits, electric service comes from a cooperative — Bandera Electric Cooperative and Pedernales Electric Cooperative both serve parts of Kendall County — and water and sewer are your problem: a well and a septic system, with the capital cost and maintenance that implies.

In San Antonio you get CPS Energy and SAWS, both large municipally-owned utilities with their own rate trajectories.

Sales tax is 8.25% in Boerne — 6.25% state, 1.50% city, 0.50% county (City of Boerne). That's the Texas cap and it matches San Antonio.

Insurance. Both markets sit in a Texas homeowners insurance environment that runs well above the national average, and hail is the driving peril in this part of the state. Get an actual quote on the actual address before you commit — see the cost of living guide for more on that.

Everything else. Boerne has a real grocery, restaurant and services base for a town its size, but it does not have San Antonio's depth. Specialty medical care, major-airport access, professional sports, and the long tail of retail all live in San Antonio. If you're in Boerne, you drive down for those. That's fine — it's an hour of your Saturday — but it's a genuine cost that doesn't show up on a spreadsheet.

Lifestyle and land use

This is where the two are least alike, and it's less about "small town versus city" than about how the land is governed.

Kendall County does not have zoning. The County Engineer's office states that the county "does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas of the County," and that it "has not adopted building codes for single family residential developments" (Kendall County Engineer verification letter, March 4, 2026). The county does permit driveways, work in county right-of-way, outdoor lighting, on-site sewage facilities, floodplain development and site improvements, and has adopted a Fire Code administered by the Fire Marshal.

Cut both ways:

  • For you: you can build a shop, keep animals, run a business from a barn, and generally use your land without asking permission from a planning commission.
  • Against you: so can your neighbor. Your only protection is the subdivision's deed restrictions and HOA. Read them before you buy, and read them for what they permit as much as what they forbid.

Inside Boerne city limits, you get the opposite: a Unified Development Code, zoning, a building department, and a dark-sky lighting ordinance. Predictability, at the cost of flexibility.

San Antonio, for all its size, is a zoned city with a code department. If you want to know what can be built next door, there's an answer. In unincorporated Kendall County, often there isn't one.

Where San Antonio genuinely wins

I sell in both markets and I'd be doing you a disservice if I only argued one side.

Budget under about $450,000. Boerne's inventory at that price is thin and getting thinner. San Antonio has real choice.

A downtown, South Side or east-side job. The commute math stops working.

You want walkable urban. Boerne's downtown is genuinely charming and genuinely small. Southtown, Alamo Heights, Olmos Park and King William offer an urban life Boerne does not.

You need frequent specialty medical care. Proximity to the Medical Center is worth more than a lower tax rate.

You want maximum liquidity. San Antonio's deeper buyer pool means a faster, more predictable resale, particularly in the mid-market. A $1.4 million acreage property in Kendall County has a small buyer pool and can take a long time to sell.

You're a short-term investor. At 3% annual appreciation and a 6% cost of sale, neither market rewards a two-year hold, but Boerne's thinner resale market makes a fast exit harder.

The short version

Buy Boerne if you want the school district, the land, the lower effective tax rate, and a small-town base — and you're planning to be here five or more years. Buy San Antonio if your budget, your job location, or your need for urban density says so. Both are defensible. What isn't defensible is picking based on a rate comparison somebody ran without the exemptions in it.

Genuinely torn? Send me the two addresses you're weighing — one in each — and I'll run the real numbers on both: verified tax rate for each parcel, school zone confirmed with the district, MUD status, utility situation, and the total monthly cost of ownership side by side. I'll tell you if San Antonio is the better buy for your situation. I sell in both.

Call or text 830-446-3847 · Email heath.shepard@kw.com

Heath Shepard, REALTOR — Keller Williams, Boerne and San Antonio. Eleven years in Texas real estate, with a background in land development.

title: Boerne ISD Schools Guide
metaTitle: Boerne ISD Schools Guide: Ratings, Campuses, Boundaries and Home Value
metaDescription: Boerne ISD earned an A (score 92) from TEA in 2026 — its seventh straight. Campus list, attendance zone traps, and how schools move home values here.
summary: Boerne ISD earned an A with an overall score of 92 in the TEA ratings released August 2026 — its seventh consecutive A, with a 99.2% graduation rate. A Boerne mailing address does not guarantee Boerne ISD; western and northern Kendall County is Comfort ISD. Verify the campus with Administrative Services at (830) 357-2011.
body:
If you are buying in Boerne for the schools — and a large share of buyers here are — this is the page you need before you tour anything. The district rating is excellent and verifiable. The part that costs people money is the attendance zone, not the rating.

The current rating, with the actual numbers

In the Texas Education Agency accountability ratings released in August 2026, covering the 2025-26 school year, Boerne ISD earned an A with an overall score of 92. The domain breakdown:

Domain Score
Student Achievement 93
School Progress 83
Closing the Gaps 90
Overall 92 (A)

The district also reported a 99.2% graduation rate and college, career and military readiness at 98% (Boerne Star, August 19, 2026). This was the district's seventh consecutive A rating.

In the prior cycle — the 2025 ratings released in August 2025 — Boerne ISD also earned an A, its sixth consecutive, along with 27 distinction designations (Community Impact, August 15, 2025).

Two things worth understanding about what that rating is and isn't:

School Progress at 83 is the number to watch. In TEA's system, Student Achievement measures absolute performance and School Progress measures growth. A district with a strong, affluent, well-supported student body tends to score high on achievement almost automatically. Growth is harder. An 83 against a 93 achievement score is the honest read on what the district is doing for students versus what the students bring with them. It is a good score. It is not the same score.

A district rating is not a campus rating. TEA rates individual campuses as well as districts, and campus ratings within an A district are not uniform. I am not going to publish individual campus scores here without pulling them directly, and neither should anyone else. Check the current campus rating for the specific school your address feeds into at TxSchools.gov before you make a decision on it. If you want, send me the address and I'll pull it.

The campuses

Boerne ISD's campuses, per the district:

Elementary

  • Cibolo Creek Elementary
  • Curington Elementary
  • Fabra Elementary
  • Fair Oaks Ranch Elementary
  • Herff Elementary
  • Kendall Elementary
  • Van Raub Elementary
  • Viola Wilson Elementary

Middle

  • Boerne Middle School North
  • Boerne Middle School South
  • Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School

High

  • Boerne High School
  • Champion High School
  • Boerne Academy

The attendance zone trap — read this twice

This is where Boerne buyers get burned, and it happens several times a year.

A Boerne mailing address does not mean Boerne ISD. The western and northern portions of Kendall County are served by Comfort ISD, a separate district with its own rating and its own tax rate (0.9328 for 2025 versus Boerne ISD's 1.0109, per Kendall Appraisal District). Properties with Boerne postal addresses fall into Comfort ISD regularly.

Boerne ISD extends beyond Kendall County. The City of Fair Oaks Ranch spans Kendall, Comal and Bexar counties, and is served by Boerne ISD and — for Comal County residents — Comal ISD (City of Fair Oaks Ranch). So a Boerne ISD home can be appraised by Kendall Appraisal District, Comal Appraisal District or Bexar Appraisal District, each with a different county tax rate. On a Fair Oaks Ranch street, the school district and the county can both change between one house and the next.

The district's own guidance is explicit: "homes located near the school district boundary lines must be verified by the Administrative Services Department." The district provides an InfoFinder tool where you enter a street address and zip code to see assigned schools and bus stops, and Administrative Services can be reached at (830) 357-2011.

Here is my rule, and I don't bend it: for any address within about a mile of a boundary, I get written confirmation from the district before my client writes an offer. Not the MLS listing. Not a third-party school-search site. Not the seller's recollection. The district, in writing.

Third-party school sites are wrong often enough that relying on them is negligence. MLS school fields are entered by agents and are not verified by anyone.

Boundaries move — plan for it

Boerne ISD is a fast-growth district, and fast-growth districts redraw boundaries. The Board of Trustees approved new elementary attendance boundaries in April 2024, creating an attendance zone for Viola Wilson Elementary and providing enrollment relief at Fabra, Kendall and Van Raub Elementary.

The practical implication: if you're buying specifically to attend a particular campus, understand that the assignment is a current condition, not a permanent feature of the property. That's true anywhere, but it's more true in a district adding students every year.

What you can rely on more durably is the district itself. District-level boundaries don't move; campus assignments within them do.

How schools actually affect home value here

Three mechanisms, in descending order of how much they matter.

1. The district premium is real and it's the dominant one

The Boerne ISD rating is the reason families cross the Kendall County line. It shows up as a willingness to pay more and to accept a longer commute. That premium attaches to the district, not to a specific campus, which is why a campus reassignment is less damaging to value than buyers fear.

2. Campus-level premiums exist but are smaller and noisier

Within a strong district, campus-to-campus price differences are driven as much by the age and price point of the surrounding housing stock as by the school. A newer subdivision feeding a newer campus prices higher — and it is very hard to separate "the school" from "the houses are newer."

Be skeptical of anyone who tells you a specific elementary is worth a precise dollar premium. The data here is too thin to support that claim honestly.

3. The tax that funds it

This runs the other way and buyers underweight it.

Boerne ISD's 2025 adopted rate is 1.0109 per $100. That is the largest single line on a Boerne tax bill — roughly 54% of a combined in-city rate of 1.8645, and 73% of an unincorporated rate of 1.3929 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 adopted rates).

The district's rate history tells you something useful:

Tax year Boerne ISD rate School homestead exemption
2020 1.2519 $25,000
2021 1.2046 $25,000
2022 1.1786 $40,000
2023 0.9932 $100,000
2024 0.9909 $100,000
2025 1.0109 $140,000

(Kendall Appraisal District, Boerne ISD adopted tax rates and exemptions)

The rate came down substantially from 2020 to 2024 through state compression, and the homestead exemption went from $25,000 to $140,000 over the same span. The 2025 rate ticked back up two cents.

That increase was a voter-approval tax rate election. Boerne ISD's 1.0109 rate was adopted contingent on voter approval at a November 4, 2025 election; the district's published rate sheet carried an asterisk reading "Pending Voter Approval — Election Date 11/4/2025" until the result was certified. It passed, and was canvassed November 18, 2025. It generates about $4.8 million — roughly $3 million local plus $1.8 million in state funding — with more than 80% going to compensation, including raising the teacher minimum starting salary from $55,142 to $60,000, auxiliary minimum wage to $15 an hour and paraprofessional minimum to $16 an hour (Community Impact, November 18, 2025).

Underwrite your escrow accordingly. A fast-growth district with rising enrollment will keep going back to voters, for both operating rates and bonds. Assuming today's rate is a permanent ceiling is how people end up with an escrow shortage letter in year two.

Scale, for context

Boerne ISD's 2025 certified appraisal roll covers 24,924 taxable property accounts with a total market value of $14.74 billion and a net taxable value of $8.93 billion, producing an approximate levy of $80.3 million at the 1.0109 rate. Of those accounts, 11,664 carry a residence homestead exemption and 4,772 over-65 accounts are under a tax ceiling freeze (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals, as of Supplement 47, December 3, 2025).

The freeze matters for planning. Once a qualifying over-65 homeowner's ceiling is set, further rate or value increases don't raise their school tax. With nearly 4,800 frozen accounts in the district and an aging population, a growing share of the burden of each new rate increase falls on non-frozen accounts — which means younger families with children in those schools.

The short checklist

Before you make an offer on a house you're buying for Boerne ISD:

  1. Confirm the assigned campus with Boerne ISD Administrative Services, in writing.
  2. Confirm the county the parcel sits in — especially anywhere near Fair Oaks Ranch.
  3. Pull the current campus rating at TxSchools.gov, not the district rating.
  4. Get the exact combined tax rate for the parcel, including any MUD.
  5. Ask whether the neighborhood was affected by, or is likely to be affected by, a boundary study.

Send me the address. I'll verify the school zone with the district directly, pull the current campus rating, confirm which county and appraisal district the parcel is in, and give you the exact combined tax rate. It takes me ten minutes and it's the single highest-value thing I can do for a family buying here for the schools.

Call or text 830-446-3847 · Email heath.shepard@kw.com

Heath Shepard, REALTOR — Keller Williams, Boerne and San Antonio. Eleven years in Texas real estate, with a background in land development.

title: Cost of Living in Boerne, TX
metaTitle: Cost of Living in Boerne, TX: Taxes, Utilities, Insurance and HOA
metaDescription: What it actually costs to own in Boerne TX: verified 2025 tax rates, city utility bills, well and septic costs, insurance reality and HOA questions.
summary: The largest variable is jurisdiction: on the roughly $602,600 median, 2025 annual property tax runs about $6,978 unincorporated, $9,820 inside city limits, $13,004 in Miralomas MUD. Neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general homestead exemption — only the $140,000 school exemption, worth roughly $1,415 a year. Sales tax is 8.25%.
body:
Most cost-of-living calculators are useless for Boerne, because they index against a city average and Boerne isn't one place. The single biggest variable in your monthly cost of ownership is whether your parcel sits inside Boerne city limits, in unincorporated Kendall County, or inside a municipal utility district. That one fact can swing your housing cost by several hundred dollars a month on an identical house.

Here's what I can document.

Property tax: the biggest line

Adopted rates for tax year 2025, per Kendall Appraisal District:

Entity Rate per $100
Boerne ISD 1.0109
Comfort ISD 0.9328
City of Boerne 0.4716
Kendall County 0.3770
Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District 0.0050
Kendall County MUD #1 0.6500
Miralomas MUD 1.0000
Kendall County WCID #1 0.166106

Combined, as published by the appraisal district:

Jurisdiction stack Combined rate
City of Boerne + Kendall County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek 1.8645
Kendall County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek (unincorporated) 1.3929
Above + Kendall County MUD #1 2.0429
Above + Miralomas MUD 2.3929
Kendall County + Comfort ISD + Cow Creek 1.3148
Above + Kendall County WCID #1 1.480906

The exemption fact almost nobody tells you

Neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general residence homestead exemption. Kendall County offers $10,000 for over-65 and disabled persons. The City of Boerne offers a tax ceiling freeze for qualifying over-65 and disabled homesteads but no general homestead reduction (Kendall Appraisal District, adopted tax rates and exemptions).

The only general homestead exemption on a Boerne tax bill is the state-mandated school district exemption of $140,000, which appears at both Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD on the district's published exemption schedule.

That is meaningfully less generous than Bexar County, where the county, the city, the hospital district, the community college district and the river authority each offer their own local homestead exemption. If you're moving from San Antonio, do not assume your exemption savings will scale.

What that means in dollars

On the median Boerne-area sale price of about $602,600 (as of September 2026, per SABOR MLS), with a general residence homestead exemption:

Location Annual tax Monthly escrow
Unincorporated Kendall County, Boerne ISD $6,978 ~$582
Inside Boerne city limits, Boerne ISD $9,820 ~$818
Unincorporated, Kendall County MUD #1 $10,895 ~$908
Unincorporated, Miralomas MUD $13,004 ~$1,084
Unincorporated Kendall County, Comfort ISD $6,617 ~$551

Calculated from 2025 adopted rates published by Kendall Appraisal District, with the $140,000 school homestead exemption and no other exemptions applied.

The homestead exemption itself is worth about $1,415 a year at the Boerne ISD rate — meaningful, but not the multi-thousand-dollar reduction people expect. File it anyway; it also starts your 10% annual appraisal cap.

Sales tax

8.25% in Boerne: 6.25% state, 1.50% city, 0.50% county (City of Boerne). That's the Texas statutory maximum and it matches San Antonio. No advantage either direction.

Boerne's hotel occupancy tax is 7% city on top of 6% state — relevant if you're operating a short-term rental, irrelevant if you're not.

Utilities

Inside city limits

The City of Boerne owns and operates six utilities: electric, natural gas, water, wastewater, stormwater and reclaimed water. One provider, one bill, rates set by City Council.

What I can document on cost: in February 2025, the average residential water-and-wastewater bill moved from $90.46 to $94.71 per month. The base charge rose about 7% — a 5/8-inch connection went from $28.11 to $30.08, and a 3/4-inch connection from $58.58 to $62.68. The City has indicated further increases over a five-year horizon to fund its Boerne Utilities Capital Improvement Plan (Community Impact, February 3, 2025).

Note the meter-size detail, because it matters and buyers miss it. A 3/4-inch meter carries roughly double the base charge of a 5/8-inch meter before you use a single gallon. Larger and newer homes frequently have larger meters. Ask what meter is on the house.

Electric and gas rates vary by customer classification. Get the actual twelve-month utility history from the seller during your option period — it is a far better predictor than any average, and on a house with a pool, a well pump or a detached shop it will be substantially higher than the city average.

Outside city limits

No city utilities. Electric service comes from a cooperative — Bandera Electric Cooperative and Pedernales Electric Cooperative both serve portions of Kendall County. The City's own electric service area is defined by the Public Utility Commission and covers most of the city limits plus some areas beyond it, so the boundary is not simply the city line. Verify who serves the specific address.

Water is a well or a water supply corporation. Sewer is a septic system. Propane replaces natural gas in most rural locations.

Budget for rural infrastructure as a capital item, not a utility bill:

  • Well pump replacement is a real, periodic expense and it happens without warning.
  • Aerobic septic systems carry a maintenance contract with periodic inspections and ongoing cost; conventional systems need pumping on a cycle.
  • Propane is a commodity you buy in bulk and it is priced by the market, not by a regulated tariff.
  • Water hauling is a real thing during severe drought for properties with marginal wells.

Kendall County permits on-site sewage facilities and approves or denies an application within 30 days of receipt. Groundwater is managed by the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District, created by county voters in 2002; the county sits within the Hill Country Priority Groundwater Management Area over the Trinity Aquifer.

I will not publish typical dollar figures for well drilling, septic installation or propane here, because I haven't verified current local pricing and a stale number is worse than no number. Get current quotes from a local driller, installer and propane supplier — I'm happy to point you to people.

Homeowners insurance

This is the line item that has moved most in the last several years and the one buyers underbudget most badly.

Texas runs well above the national average on homeowners insurance. Published 2026 statewide estimates vary by methodology and coverage assumption, generally landing somewhere in the $3,300 to $4,900 per year range for a typical policy, with some analyses putting the statewide average above $4,000 (NerdWallet and other 2026 industry analyses). Those are statewide figures, not Boerne figures, and I am not going to present a Boerne-specific average I can't source.

What actually drives your number here:

  • Hail. This is the dominant peril in Central Texas and the main reason Texas premiums are high. Roof age and roof material drive your premium and sometimes your insurability. A 15-year-old composition roof can push you to an actual-cash-value roof settlement instead of replacement cost, which is a five-figure difference after a hailstorm.
  • Wildfire exposure. On heavily wooded Hill Country acreage, brush proximity and defensible space matter to underwriters and to premium.
  • Distance to a fire station and ISO protection class. Rural properties rate worse. This is a real and often large difference between an in-town house and one fifteen minutes out.
  • Water source. Some carriers treat well-and-septic properties differently.
  • Claims history on the address, not just on you. Pull the CLUE report.

Do this during your option period, not after: get a bound quote on the specific address from an agent who writes in Kendall County. Not an estimate, not a range — a quote on that address with that roof. I've seen quotes on comparable-looking Boerne properties come back thousands of dollars apart, and insurance is one of the few closing surprises that can actually kill a deal on debt-to-income.

HOA and deed restrictions

Kendall County does not have zoning in unincorporated areas, which makes HOA documents disproportionately important — they are the only land-use control on a country property.

HOA dues vary enormously across this market, from modest annual assessments in older subdivisions to substantial monthly dues in gated, amenity-heavy developments with private roads, gates, pools or golf. I'm not going to publish an "average" — the range is so wide that an average would mislead you.

What to ask for, every time, during the option period:

  1. Current dues and payment frequency, plus the assessment history for the last five years.
  2. Whether there is a special assessment pending or contemplated. Private roads are the usual source. A subdivision that maintains its own roads has a capital liability that shows up eventually.
  3. The resale certificate and transfer fees, which are paid at closing and are frequently a few hundred dollars that nobody mentioned.
  4. The full declaration of covenants, conditions and restrictions — and read it for what it permits, not just what it forbids. Can your neighbor run a business? Keep livestock? Park an RV? Build a metal shop? In the absence of county zoning, the CCRs are the answer.
  5. Whether short-term rentals are permitted. Many Kendall County subdivisions prohibit them by covenant regardless of what the city or county allows.
  6. Architectural control committee requirements, if you plan to build, add on, or put up a barn or shop.
  7. The reserve balance, if the association maintains infrastructure.

Everything else

Kendall County's median household income was reported at $105,400 and the City of Boerne's at $91,947, with median ages of 43 and 40 respectively (Boerne Kendall County Economic Development Corporation). That's a comparatively affluent base, which shows up in local retail and restaurant pricing.

Boerne has a genuine grocery, healthcare, restaurant and services base for a town of about 24,000. What it doesn't have is San Antonio's depth — specialty medical, big-box variety, major-airport access and the long tail of retail are a drive down I-10. Budget the time, not just the gas.

Want your actual number, not an average? Send me an address and I'll pull the verified combined tax rate for that exact parcel, tell you whether it's in a MUD, confirm the utility provider and water source, and flag anything in the HOA documents worth knowing before you spend money on an inspection. That's a free ten minutes from me and it's usually the difference between a budget that holds and one that doesn't.
