title: Moving to Boerne, TX: A Relocation Guide
metaTitle: Moving to Boerne, TX: A Relocation Guide for Out-of-State Buyers
metaDescription: Relocating to Boerne TX from California, Austin or out of state? The tax reset that catches everyone, wells, septic, no zoning, and a real timeline.
summary: Kendall County's population reached an estimated 53,289 in 2025, up 20.3% since 2020. The mistake relocating buyers make is underwriting off the seller's tax bill: the 10% homestead appraisal cap and any over-65 ceiling freeze reset at sale. Calculate purchase price times the parcel's combined rate, minus the $140,000 school exemption.
body:
Kendall County's population was estimated at 53,289 in 2025, up 20.3% since 2020, with domestic in-migration — people moving here from elsewhere in the U.S. — as the dominant driver (Community Impact, March 30, 2026, citing Census Bureau estimates). The City of Boerne was estimated at 24,047 as of July 2025.

You're not the first person to have this idea. You are, however, probably about to make one of about five specific mistakes that out-of-state buyers make in this county. Let's go through them.

Mistake 1: assuming the seller's tax bill is your tax bill

This is the expensive one, and it catches nearly every relocation buyer.

Texas has no state income tax. It funds local government through property tax, and property is appraised at market value annually. There are two protections, and neither one transfers to you:

The 10% homestead appraisal cap. Once you have a homestead exemption in place, your appraised value can rise no more than 10% per year plus the value of new improvements. A homeowner who bought in 2015 may be assessed far below market today. In Boerne ISD alone, that cap removed $543 million of value from the 2025 roll (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals).

The over-65 tax ceiling freeze. Kendall County, the City of Boerne, Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD all offer a tax freeze for qualifying over-65 or disabled homesteads. Boerne ISD's 2025 roll shows 4,772 over-65 accounts under a ceiling (Kendall Appraisal District).

When you buy, the cap resets and the freeze ends. The property gets reappraised to market — which, conveniently for the appraisal district, is the price you just paid. If you're buying from a long-tenured owner or a senior under a freeze, your first full-year tax bill can be dramatically higher than the tax figure on the MLS listing.

Never, ever underwrite off the current tax bill. Underwrite off your purchase price times the parcel's combined rate, minus the $140,000 school homestead exemption. I run that number for every buyer before they write an offer, and I recommend you make any agent you work with do the same.

The actual math

Combined 2025 rates, per Kendall Appraisal District:

Location Combined rate Tax on a $602,600 home w/ homestead
Unincorporated Kendall County, Boerne ISD 1.3929 ~$6,978
Inside Boerne city limits, Boerne ISD 1.8645 ~$9,820
Kendall County MUD #1 2.0429 ~$10,895
Miralomas MUD 2.3929 ~$13,004

For California buyers specifically

Your instinct from Proposition 13 is that acquisition value locks in and grows slowly. Texas is the opposite: annual reappraisal at market, with a 10% cap that only applies once you have a homestead exemption and only to a homestead. There is no acquisition-value lock.

The offset is that Texas has no state income tax, and for a high earner that is frequently a larger number than the property tax difference. Run both, together, with your CPA. Do not run either one alone.

For Austin buyers

You already understand Texas property tax. What's different is the exemption structure. Neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general residence homestead exemption (Kendall Appraisal District). Your only general homestead exemption here is the $140,000 school district exemption. Check what your current taxing entities offer before you assume it's a wash.

Mistake 2: assuming a Boerne address means Boerne ISD and Kendall County

Three separate traps live here, and all three are common.

Comfort ISD. The western and northern parts of Kendall County are served by Comfort ISD, not Boerne ISD — different rating, different rate (0.9328 vs. 1.0109 for 2025). Plenty of Comfort ISD homes have Boerne mailing addresses.

Fair Oaks Ranch. The City of Fair Oaks Ranch spans Kendall, Comal and Bexar counties. Property is appraised by Kendall Appraisal District, Comal Appraisal District or Bexar Appraisal District depending on the parcel, and the city is served by Boerne ISD and, for Comal County residents, Comal ISD. City property taxes are billed by the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector regardless of which county you live in (City of Fair Oaks Ranch). Two houses on the same street can be in different counties and different school districts.

Boundary proximity. Boerne ISD's own guidance is that homes near district boundary lines "must be verified by the Administrative Services Department." Get it in writing. The district can be reached at (830) 357-2011.

Boerne ISD earned an A with an overall score of 92 in the TEA ratings released in August 2026 — its seventh consecutive A, with a 99.2% graduation rate (Boerne Star, August 19, 2026). That rating is a big part of why you're reading this page. Make sure you're actually buying into it.

Mistake 3: buying rural without understanding what rural means here

Roughly two-thirds of the taxable property in Boerne ISD sits outside Boerne city limits — the district covers 24,924 accounts while the city covers 9,157 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals). If you're picturing land, you're picturing unincorporated Kendall County. Here's what that actually entails.

Water is a well. Kendall County sits in the Hill Country Priority Groundwater Management Area over the Trinity Aquifer, and the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District was created by county voters in 2002 to manage it. A well needs a yield test, a water quality test, registration status confirmed, and — honestly — a conversation with the neighbors about how it performed in the last serious drought. A well that's fine in March and marginal in August is the classic failure mode.

Sewer is a septic system. Kendall County permits on-site sewage facilities and approves or denies applications within 30 days of receipt. For an existing house, get the permit, the design, the service history, and a dedicated septic inspection — not the general inspector's quick look. For vacant land, the whole deal depends on whether a system can be permitted, and only a licensed site evaluator can tell you.

Nobody inspected the house. The Kendall County Engineer's office states the county "has not adopted building codes for single family residential developments" in the unincorporated areas. The county does permit driveways, work in county right-of-way, outdoor lighting, floodplain development, on-site sewage facilities and site improvements, and it has adopted a Fire Code administered by the Fire Marshal — but a single-family house built in the county was not inspected by a municipal building department. Your third-party inspection is the entire quality-control system. Budget for specialists.

There is no zoning. The same letter states the county "does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas of the County." Your only protection against what happens next door is the subdivision's deed restrictions and HOA. Read them before you buy — for what they permit as well as what they forbid.

Outdoor lighting is regulated. Kendall County requires a permit before installing any outdoor lights and requires International Dark-Sky Association compliant products. The City of Boerne has its own dark-sky regulations in its Unified Development Code. This is a genuinely nice feature of living here — the night sky is worth the trouble — but check before you budget for lighting.

Mistake 4: underbudgeting insurance

Texas homeowners insurance runs well above the national average, and hail is the driving reason. Roof age and material will drive your premium and can affect whether you're written at replacement cost or actual cash value. Rural properties rate worse on distance-to-fire-station. Wooded acreage draws wildfire underwriting scrutiny.

Get a bound quote on the specific address during your option period, from an agent who writes in Kendall County. Not a range, not an online estimate — a real quote on that roof at that address. I've seen quotes on similar-looking properties come back thousands apart, and insurance is one of the few surprises that can break a deal on debt-to-income at the last minute.

Mistake 5: not driving the commute

If you'll be commuting into San Antonio, drive it on a Tuesday at 7:15 a.m. before you commit. The corridor is I-10, TxDOT has been reworking it in stages for years, and the experience differs enormously depending on whether you're headed to the northwest employment corridor or downtown. A commute that's pleasant on a Sunday afternoon can be a different life at 7:15 on a weekday.

The timeline that actually works

Three to six months out

  • Get pre-approved with a lender who does rural lending in Kendall County. Acreage, outbuildings and thin comp sets create appraisal and product issues that a generic online lender will discover too late.
  • Decide the fundamental question: in town or on land. They are different purchases with different diligence, different costs, and different resale profiles.
  • Pull tax estimates at your target price for the jurisdictions you're considering.

Two to three months out

  • Come for a scouting trip. Drive the commute. Drive it at rush hour.
  • Tour in-town and acreage on the same trip so you can feel the difference rather than theorize about it.
  • If schools matter, visit the campuses and verify the zones with the district.

Under contract

  • Order the survey the day the option period starts.
  • Schedule inspection, septic inspection and well testing immediately. Rural inspectors book further out than city ones — negotiate a longer option period on a country property for exactly this reason.
  • Get the bound insurance quote.
  • Read the HOA documents and the title commitment's Schedule B in full.
  • One scheduling note that costs people money: if your contract executes Wednesday through Friday, part of your option period runs while the title company is closed. Under a short option that's a real problem. Push execution earlier in the week when you can.

After closing

  • File your homestead exemption. The general deadline for filing an exemption application is before May 1 (Texas Comptroller). A buyer who acquires property after January 1 may receive the residence homestead exemption for the applicable portion of that tax year immediately upon qualifying, if the prior owner didn't already have it for that year (Kendall Appraisal District, March 2026). Filing is free — do it yourself and ignore anyone who mails you an offer to file it for a fee.
  • Put May 15 on your calendar for protest season. See the property tax guide for how that works.
  • Register your well with Cow Creek GCD if it isn't already.

What I'd want you to know that isn't on a spreadsheet

Boerne is a small town that is growing fast, and it feels like both of those things at once. Downtown is genuinely walkable and genuinely charming, and it is also genuinely small. People are friendly in a way that surprises coastal transplants and they are also aware that a lot of new people are arriving. Showing up curious goes a long way.

The Hill Country is beautiful and it is hard country. It floods fast, it droughts hard, cedar pollen in winter is real, and the deer will eat every plant you own. None of that is a reason not to come. It is a reason to buy with your eyes open rather than off a photograph.

Relocating from out of state? Send me your target price, your commute destination, and whether you're picturing a neighborhood or land. I'll come back with real tax numbers for the specific areas that fit, an honest read on the commute, and the two or three sub-markets worth your scouting trip. I do this for out-of-state buyers regularly and I'd rather you spend your trip efficiently than drive around figuring out the county lines.

Call or text 830-446-3847 · Email heath.shepard@kw.com

Heath Shepard, REALTOR — Keller Williams, Boerne and San Antonio. Eleven years in Texas real estate, with a background in land development.

title: Boerne Property Taxes Explained
metaTitle: Boerne Property Taxes Explained: Rates, Exemptions and How to Protest
metaDescription: Every Kendall County tax rate, every exemption, the 10% cap, ag valuation and the protest process — with the real 2025 numbers from the appraisal district.
summary: Boerne is in Kendall County, not Bexar. Tax year 2025 adopted rates: Boerne ISD 1.0109, City of Boerne 0.4716, Kendall County 0.3770, Cow Creek GCD 0.0050 — 1.8645 combined inside city limits, 1.3929 unincorporated. Neither the city nor the county offers a general homestead exemption; only the $140,000 school exemption applies. Protest by May 15.
body:
Everything below comes from the Kendall Appraisal District's own published rate and exemption schedules and its 2025 certified appraisal roll. No estimates, no "approximately."

Start here: Boerne is in Kendall County. It is not in Bexar County and it is not part of the City of San Antonio. If you're reading a property tax article about "San Antonio area" rates, exemptions, or ordinances, it does not describe your Boerne bill.

Who taxes a Boerne property

Adopted rates for tax year 2025, per Kendall Appraisal District:

Taxing entity Code Rate per $100 Homestead Over-65 Disabled
Boerne ISD SBN 1.0109 $140,000 $60,000 $60,000
Comfort ISD SCF 0.9328 $140,000 $60,000 $60,000
City of Boerne CBN 0.4716 — — —
Kendall County GKE 0.3770 — $10,000 $10,000
Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District WCC 0.0050 — — —
Kendall County MUD #1 MCD 0.6500 — — —
Miralomas MUD MML 1.0000 — — —
Kendall County WCID #1 WCF 0.166106 — — —

All entities offer the state disabled veteran partial exemptions: DV1 $5,000, DV2 $7,500, DV3 $10,000, DV4 $12,000.

A tax ceiling freeze is offered by the City of Boerne, Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD and Kendall County for a qualifying homestead with an over-65 or disabled person exemption.

Combined rates, as published by the appraisal district

Jurisdiction stack Combined rate
City of Boerne + County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek 1.864500
County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek (unincorporated) 1.392900
County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek + MUD #1 2.042900
County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek + Miralomas MUD 2.392900
County + Comfort ISD + Cow Creek 1.314800
County + Comfort ISD + Cow Creek + WCID #1 1.480906

The single biggest lever on your Boerne tax bill is whether the parcel is inside city limits. On the median area sale price of about $602,600 (as of September 2026, per SABOR MLS), the City of Boerne's 0.4716 rate is $2,841.86 a year — about $237 a month of escrow.

The exemption fact that surprises everyone

Neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general residence homestead exemption. Look at the table above: the homestead column is blank for both. Kendall County offers $10,000 for over-65 and disabled persons. The City of Boerne offers a freeze for qualifying over-65 and disabled homesteads but no general homestead reduction.

The only general homestead exemption on your Boerne bill is the state-mandated $140,000 school district exemption, reflected at both Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD on the appraisal district's published schedule.

That is a real difference from Bexar County, where the county, the city, the hospital district, the community college district and the river authority each offer their own local homestead exemption. If you're relocating from San Antonio, don't assume your exemption savings scale.

What the homestead exemption is actually worth here

$140,000 × 1.0109% = $1,415.26 a year. That's it — the school district piece is the whole benefit.

File it anyway, for a second reason that matters more over time: the homestead exemption is what starts your 10% annual appraisal cap.

The rate history

Boerne ISD (Kendall Appraisal District):

Tax year Rate School homestead exemption
2016 1.3160 $25,000
2017 1.3540 $25,000
2018 1.3540 $25,000
2019 1.2840 $25,000
2020 1.2519 $25,000
2021 1.2046 $25,000
2022 1.1786 $40,000
2023 0.9932 $100,000
2024 0.9909 $100,000
2025 1.0109 $140,000

City of Boerne: 0.4720 from 2016 through 2021, 0.4510 in 2022, 0.4766 in 2023, and 0.4716 in both 2024 and 2025.

Kendall County: 0.3940 in 2016, 0.4127 from 2017 through 2021, 0.3877 in 2022, 0.3827 in 2023 and 2024, and 0.3770 in 2025 — a decrease approved by Commissioners Court in August 2025 (Community Impact, August 27, 2025).

The 2025 Boerne ISD increase was a voter-approval tax rate election. The district's published rate sheet carried an asterisk — "Pending Voter Approval — Election Date 11/4/2025" — until the result was certified. It passed and was canvassed November 18, 2025, generating about $4.8 million ($3 million local, $1.8 million state), with more than 80% going to compensation, including raising the teacher minimum starting salary from $55,142 to $60,000 (Community Impact, November 18, 2025).

Worked examples

All on a $602,600 assessed value with only the general residence homestead exemption:

Inside Boerne city limits, Boerne ISD

  • Boerne ISD: ($602,600 − $140,000) × 1.0109% = $4,676.43
  • City of Boerne: $602,600 × 0.4716% = $2,841.86
  • Kendall County: $602,600 × 0.3770% = $2,271.80
  • Cow Creek GCD: $602,600 × 0.0050% = $30.13
  • Total: $9,820.22 — an effective rate of 1.63%

Unincorporated Kendall County, Boerne ISD

  • Boerne ISD: $4,676.43
  • Kendall County: $2,271.80
  • Cow Creek GCD: $30.13
  • Total: $6,978.36 — an effective rate of 1.16%

Same house, no homestead exemption (second home or rental), in city limits

  • $602,600 × 1.8645% = $11,235.48

In Miralomas MUD, with homestead

  • $6,978.36 + ($602,600 × 1.0000% = $6,026.00) = $13,004.36

Exemptions, one by one

General residence homestead — $140,000 (school districts)

Texas Tax Code 11.13(b) requires school districts to provide a $140,000 residence homestead exemption (Texas Comptroller). Kendall Appraisal District's adopted exemption schedule reflects $140,000 at Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD for tax year 2025, up from $100,000 in 2024 and $40,000 in 2022.

A homestead is generally the home and land used as the owner's principal residence on January 1 of the tax year. Important for buyers: a person who acquires property after January 1 may receive the residence homestead exemption for the applicable portion of that tax year immediately upon qualifying, if the preceding owner did not already receive the same exemption for that year (Kendall Appraisal District, March 2026).

The general deadline for filing an exemption application is before May 1 (Texas Comptroller). It is free. If you get a letter offering to file it for you for a fee, throw it away.

Over-65 and disabled person

An additional $60,000 school district exemption under Tax Code 11.13(c), plus $10,000 from Kendall County. The City of Boerne offers no additional amount but does offer a freeze.

The tax ceiling freeze is the more valuable piece for most seniors. Once set, further rate or value increases don't raise your tax for that entity. Boerne ISD's 2025 roll shows 4,772 over-65 accounts under a ceiling and the City of Boerne's shows 1,466 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals).

The freeze does not transfer to a buyer. If you're buying from a senior under a freeze, your bill will be materially different from theirs.

Disabled veteran

Partial exemptions by disability rating: DV1 $5,000, DV2 $7,500, DV3 $10,000, DV4 $12,000, offered by every entity in the county.

Separately, Texas law provides a 100 percent homestead exemption for 100 percent disabled veterans and their surviving spouses, as well as for surviving spouses of service members killed or fatally injured in the line of duty (Kendall Appraisal District, March 2026).

This is a significant feature of the Boerne market. Boerne ISD's 2025 certified roll shows 713 accounts under the 100% disabled veteran homestead exemption, worth $354.6 million in exempted value, plus 37 surviving-spouse accounts worth $10.2 million. If you're a disabled veteran considering Boerne, this exemption should be part of your math from the beginning.

Agricultural and wildlife management valuation

This is the largest single tax feature in Kendall County and it gets almost no coverage.

Boerne ISD's 2025 roll shows $1.98 billion in agricultural market value appraised at $9.2 million under productivity valuation — a productivity loss of $1.97 billion (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals). A great deal of this county is still ranch land carrying a 1-d-1 open-space valuation.

Qualifying, per the Kendall County Ag Use Manual:

  • The land must have been used principally for agriculture for five of the preceding seven years.
  • Cow/calf: minimum of 3 calves and 10 acres.
  • Sheep: ewes plus one ram on 10 acres. Goats: 6 does and a buck, minimum 10 acres.
  • Exotics: minimum 10 acres with wire mesh fencing.
  • Beekeeping: not less than 5 nor more than 20 acres, minimum of 6 hives.
  • Orchard, vineyard or market garden: minimum 3 acres. Family gardens do not qualify.
  • Wildlife management: a minimum of three approved practices, with the land already qualified under 1-d-1.

Stocking rates are set by range type: Improved Grass Range 1 animal unit per 5 acres; Native Range I 1 AU per 10 acres; Native Range II 1 AU per 25 acres; Native Range III (oak) 1 AU per 35 acres; Native Range III (cedar) 1 AU per 50 acres.

Buyer warning: if you buy land with an ag valuation and don't continue a qualifying use, you can trigger a rollback of back taxes. Decide before closing whether you intend to maintain it, and get your plan in front of the appraisal district.

The caps

10% homestead appraisal cap

Once a residence homestead exemption is in place, appraised value can rise no more than 10% per year plus the value of new improvements. In Boerne ISD alone, this removed $543.2 million of value from the 2025 roll.

It applies only to homesteads, and it resets when the property sells. That reset is the single most common source of first-year tax shock for buyers here.

The 20% non-homestead circuit breaker (Tax Code 23.231)

Texas SB 2 (2023) created a temporary 20% annual appraisal cap on non-homestead real property at or below an indexed value threshold — $5,000,000 for 2024, $5,160,000 for 2025 and $5,320,000 for 2026. It applies to rental homes, commercial property and other investment real estate. It expires December 31, 2026 unless the legislature renews it.

In Boerne ISD, it removed $68.6 million of value from the 2025 roll — smaller than the homestead cap, but real if you own rentals here.

If you hold non-homestead property in Kendall County, watch this. Its expiration would be a meaningful change to your 2027 tax exposure.

Deferrals

Two exist and both are underused:

  • Residence homestead tax deferral: pay tax on 105% of the preceding year's appraised value plus taxes on new improvements; the remainder is deferred with interest accruing at 8% per year.
  • Over-65, disabled, or disabled veteran deferral: defer current and delinquent taxes as long as you own and live in the home, with interest accruing at 5% per year.

Both postpone taxes. Neither cancels them. Affidavits are available at the appraisal district.

How to protest

The deadline

May 15, or 30 days after your Notice of Appraised Value was mailed, whichever is later. Your notice will state the deadline for your property. If it falls on a weekend or legal holiday it moves to the next business day.

Kendall Appraisal District accepts protests through its online portal at eprotest.kendallad.org, and by mail, in person or drop box.

The steps

1. Get the district's evidence. You are entitled to the information the appraisal district used to value your property. Ask for it before your hearing, not at it.

2. Request an informal meeting. Property owners can request an informal meeting with appraisal district staff to try to resolve the dispute before an ARB hearing. A large share of protests are settled here, and it is far less work than a hearing.

3. The ARB hearing. A written protest must identify the owner, the property, and the reasons for dissatisfaction. The district publishes its ARB hearing procedures each year.

4. If you're not satisfied: binding arbitration, an appeal to district court, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings. There is also limited binding arbitration, which compels the ARB or chief appraiser to comply with a procedural requirement.

What actually works

  • Unequal appraisal beats market-value arguments more often than owners expect. If comparable properties are appraised lower, that's a statutory ground.
  • Condition evidence wins. Photographs of a failing roof, foundation movement, an outdated kitchen, or deferred maintenance are concrete. Contractor bids are better than photographs.
  • A recent purchase price below the appraised value is strong evidence. Bring the closing statement.
  • Bad property characteristics in the district's records — wrong square footage, a pool that doesn't exist, a finished-out space that isn't — are the easiest wins available and they're common. Pull your property record card at esearch.kendallad.org and read it line by line.
  • Protest every year. The cap protects you from a 30% increase; it does not stop a 10% increase compounding annually.

Contact

Kendall Appraisal District 118 Market Avenue, Boerne, TX 78006 (830) 249-8012 · requestinfo@kendallad.org Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Property search: esearch.kendallad.org · Protests and exemptions: eprotest.kendallad.org · Interactive map: gis.bisclient.com/kendallcad

Common questions

Is Boerne in Bexar County? No. Boerne is in Kendall County. Property is appraised by the Kendall Appraisal District. San Antonio and Bexar County rates, exemptions and ordinances do not apply.

Why is my tax bill so much higher than the seller's was? Because the 10% homestead appraisal cap and any over-65 ceiling freeze reset when the property sells. The property is reappraised to market — typically the price you just paid. Never underwrite off the prior owner's bill.

Does Kendall County offer a homestead exemption? Not a general one. Kendall County offers $10,000 for over-65 and disabled persons. The City of Boerne offers a freeze for qualifying over-65 and disabled homesteads but no general homestead reduction. Your general homestead exemption here comes entirely from the school district.

When is the homestead exemption deadline? The general deadline for filing an exemption application is before May 1. It is free to file.

When are taxes due? Tax statements go out in the fall and become delinquent February 1 of the following year. Confirm exact dates with the Kendall County Tax Assessor-Collector.

Should I hire a protest company? Sometimes. They typically take a percentage of your savings. On a straightforward residential protest with good condition evidence, most owners can do it themselves through the informal meeting. On a complex property, an unequal-appraisal argument, or if you simply won't do it otherwise, a professional beats not protesting.

Buying in Boerne and want the real tax number before you write an offer? Send me the address. I'll pull the exact combined rate for that parcel, confirm whether it's in a MUD or a WCID, check whether an ag valuation is in place and what a rollback would look like, and calculate your actual first-year bill after the cap resets — not the number on the listing.

I’m a 100% disabled veteran myself — if the DV exemption is part of your picture, tell me up front and I’ll run your numbers with it applied.

Call or text 830-446-3847 · Email heath.shepard@kw.com

Heath Shepard, REALTOR — Keller Williams, Boerne and San Antonio. Eleven years in Texas real estate, with a background in land development. Not a tax advisor or attorney — for tax planning, consult your CPA.

title: Short-Term Rental Rules in Boerne, TX
metaTitle: Boerne, TX Short-Term Rental Rules: What the Ordinance Actually Says
metaDescription: Boerne's STR ordinance in full: $200 permit, 200-foot block-face rule, occupancy caps, insurance, HOT registration. San Antonio's rules do not apply.
summary: San Antonio's short-term rental rules do not apply here. Boerne's Ordinance 2023-09 requires a permit for any STR inside city limits or the ETJ: $200 application, $100 inspection (ETJ exempt), two-year term. It bars operation within 200 feet of another STR on the same residential block face and caps occupancy at two per bedroom plus two.
body:
Read this first: the City of San Antonio's short-term rental ordinance does not apply in Boerne. Boerne is in Kendall County, not Bexar County, and it is a separate home-rule municipality with its own code. San Antonio's permit types, fee schedule and density rules are irrelevant here. I've watched investors underwrite a Boerne deal off a San Antonio STR guide and get the economics wrong in both directions.

What follows comes from City of Boerne Ordinance No. 2023-09, which repealed and replaced Chapter 23 of the City Code.

Where the ordinance applies

Compliance is required "before advertising, offering to rent, or renting to an occupant" any residential single-family home, residential structure, accessory dwelling, manufactured or mobile home, or duplex "located inside the area regulated by the city" for a period of less than 30 consecutive days (Sec. 23-5).

Per the City's Short-Term Rentals page, any STR operating within Boerne city limits or the city's extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ) must be registered and permitted by the City.

A short-term rental is defined as rental for compensation of any residence or residential structure, or portion of one — including a room in a home, an accessory dwelling, a manufactured/mobile home or a duplex — located in a zoning district where residential use is lawful, for overnight lodging of not more than 30 days. Hotels and motels are excluded (Sec. 23-3).

Three categories exist and they matter for how you're permitted:

  • Owner-occupied STR — the owner or tenant lives on the property and it is the owner's primary residence, "as evidenced by a current residence homestead exemption filed with the Kendall County Appraisal District."
  • Accessory dwelling / guest house STR — the owner lives on the property and rents a lawful accessory dwelling on the same lot.
  • Unoccupied STR — a stand-alone home that is not the owner's principal residence.

Permit, fees and inspection

Per Sec. 23-8:

Item Requirement
STR permit application fee $200
City safety inspection fee $100
Permit term Two years from effective date
Renewal Within 30 days after expiration; may apply 30 days prior
Inspection alternative A licensed inspector may perform it and report on the city's STR inspection checklist
ETJ properties Not required to obtain an inspection

The ordinance states these fees apply "on the effective date of this ordinance, or as subsequently amended by the city fee ordinance." Confirm the current fee schedule with the City's Planning Department at (830) 248-1501 before you budget — fee ordinances get updated and the number in a 2023 ordinance is not guaranteed to be today's number.

Other permit mechanics worth knowing:

  • Each registered STR gets a unique permit number, and that number must appear in all advertising, online or otherwise. Permit information is provided to the city police department (Sec. 23-8(e)).
  • The owner must notify the city in writing within 20 calendar days of any change to information submitted on the application (Sec. 23-8(g)).
  • Permits do not automatically transfer. A new owner may reserve the permit within 90 days of the ownership change, but must complete a new application and inspection and pay the fees. The permit cannot be moved to a different location. Before reservation, the current owner must give the new owner a Certificate of Paid Hotel Taxes from the city finance department (Sec. 23-8(h)).
  • Any owner delinquent on fees or taxes owed to the city — including hotel occupancy tax and utility service fees — is prohibited from registering until paid in full (Sec. 23-8(f)(3)).

That transfer provision is the one that bites in a transaction. If you're buying an operating STR in Boerne, the permit does not come with the house automatically. Build the 90-day reservation window, the new inspection, and the Certificate of Paid Hotel Taxes into your contract. I put this in writing during the option period on every STR purchase.

The density rule

In areas zoned for residential use:

"no short-term rental shall operate within 200 feet of another short-term rental on the same block face, measured property line to property line. Only one short-term rental may operate on any lot, property or parcel in an area zoned for residential use." (Sec. 23-7(a)(1)(a))

In the Historic, Downtown and River Road Overlay Districts:

  • Properties zoned commercial may operate an STR with no separation requirement.
  • Properties zoned residential are still subject to the 200-foot rule (Sec. 23-7(a)(1)(b)).

All other commercial zoning districts: STRs may not operate, except as permitted in the overlay provision above (Sec. 23-7(a)(1)(c)).

A special exception is available. An owner may apply to the zoning board of adjustment under Section 1.12(C) of the city's Unified Development Code. The board may consider whether operation in excess of the density limit would adversely impact residential quality, disrupt neighbors' quiet enjoyment, impact nearby streets and parking, whether the applicant wants to rent the whole residence or part of it, whether the applicant occupies the property as a primary residence or holds it as an investment, and whether other STRs beyond the separation distance already operate on that block (Sec. 23-7(a)(1)(d)).

Note the fifth factor. An owner-occupant applying for a special exception is explicitly treated differently from an investor. If you're buying purely as an investment and you need a special exception to make the deal work, understand the odds before you go hard on earnest money.

Legal nonconforming status: an STR lawfully in existence based on preexisting permits and current hotel occupancy tax remittance on the ordinance's effective date is a legal nonconforming use, and renewal or transfer of that existing permit is not subject to the minimum separation distance (Sec. 23-9(d)(1)). If you're buying an established Boerne STR, whether it carries that grandfathered status is a material question — ask, and get it confirmed by the City in writing.

Operating requirements

Occupancy (Sec. 23-7(a)(2)): two persons per bedroom, plus two additional. A three-bedroom house caps at eight. A special exception is available from the zoning board of adjustment, which may also weigh property size and fire safety.

Parking (Sec. 23-7(a)(7)): a minimum of one on-site parking space per bedroom rented. On-street parking may count if it abuts the property, is at least 25 feet long per space, and leaves clear space for a mailbox and trash receptacle.

Insurance (Sec. 23-6(b)(6)): minimum liability coverage of $500,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 in the aggregate, with an endorsement giving the city at least 30 days' notice of cancellation, non-renewal or material change — 10 days for non-payment.

Hotel occupancy tax (Sec. 23-7(a)(4)): the owner or operator must register with the city finance department to pay hotel occupancy taxes before the permit application is approved, and must remit them in a timely manner. Boerne's hotel occupancy tax is 7% city on top of the 6% state rate (City of Boerne).

Signage (Sec. 23-7(a)(3)): no signs identifying the STR, except a single nameplate not exceeding one square foot attached flat to the main building.

Advertising (Sec. 23-7(a)(11)): every listing must include the occupancy limits, parking standards, and the city permit number.

Events prohibited (Sec. 23-7(a)(10)): it is unlawful to advertise, promote or operate a special event on the premises — event center operations, banquets, weddings, receptions, reunions, parties, concerts or similar activities assembling large numbers of invitees. This kills the Hill Country wedding-venue-plus-STR business model inside the regulated area. If that's your plan, it needs a different property and a different jurisdiction.

Minimum stay (Sec. 23-7(a)(9)): no rental for less than one night.

Temporary structures prohibited (Sec. 23-7(a)(5)): no RV, tent or temporary structure of any kind may be used as an STR.

Noise (Sec. 23-7(a)(8)): city noise ordinance (Chapter 14, Article V) applies.

Well and septic (Sec. 23-7(a)(12)): if served by well and/or septic, those facilities must be maintained to meet the regulatory requirements of Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District and Kendall County specifications as applicable.

Local authorized representative: the application must name a representative with a 24-hour contact number who responds to complaints and emergency conditions including fire, natural disaster, flood, burst pipes, collapse hazard, emergency repairs and violent crime (Sec. 23-3, 23-6(b)(1)(e)).

HOA notice: the application must include confirmation that notice of STR use was provided to the HOA, if applicable (Sec. 23-6(b)(8)).

Guest information (Sec. 23-7(b)): posted in the unit and provided online — owner/operator contact, the 24-hour representative's number, neighborhood information including parking, noise, trash schedule and water restrictions, whether the property is in a floodplain, emergency contacts and weather alert instructions, and a floor plan sketch showing sleeping areas, maximum guests, evacuation routes, fire extinguisher locations and authorized parking.

Enforcement and penalties

A violation is a class C misdemeanor (Sec. 23-9(c)). Fines run up to $2,000 plus court costs for violations of regulations governing fire safety, zoning, or public health and sanitation; $4,000 plus court costs for dumping of refuse; and $500 plus court costs for all other violations. Each act of violation and each day a violation occurs is a separate offense.

Any advertisement promoting a property in the city for rent for less than 30 days is prima facie evidence of use as an STR (Sec. 23-9(b)). Operating unpermitted while listed publicly is not a defensible position.

Revocation grounds include failure to remit hotel occupancy tax within 60 days of a delinquency notice, failure to renew within 30 days, the dwelling being declared substandard, or non-collection of hotel occupancy tax for 24 months (with exceptions for renovation, use as a primary residence, or other reasonable justification). Three or more violations of the ordinance in a 12-month period, or five or more violations of other law within 24 months, can also trigger revocation. After a revocation or denial, no new permit may be sought for that property for twelve months — and the ordinance elsewhere states at least one year. Operations must stop within 10 days of notice.

Appeals go to the city manager within 20 days; the city manager must hear the appeal within 10 days and may affirm, modify or reverse. Judicial review requires filing within 30 days of the decision notice.

What about unincorporated Kendall County?

Here I'm going to give you a non-answer, on purpose.

Kendall County "does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas of the County" (Kendall County Engineer verification letter, March 4, 2026). That tells you the county has no zoning. It does not establish that the county has no short-term rental regulation, and it does not address the City of Boerne's ETJ, which extends beyond the city limits and where the City's STR ordinance does apply.

Before you underwrite a short-term rental on an unincorporated Kendall County property, call the City of Boerne Planning Department at (830) 248-1501 to confirm whether the parcel is in the ETJ, and call Kendall County to confirm what county requirements apply. Get it in writing. I'm not going to tell you a property is unregulated based on the absence of an ordinance I happened not to find.

And regardless of what the city or county says: check the deed restrictions. In a county with no zoning, subdivision covenants are the operative land-use control, and many Kendall County subdivisions prohibit short-term rentals outright.

Buying a Boerne property to short-term rent? Send me the address and I'll check whether it's in city limits, in the ETJ, or unincorporated; look at the block face for the 200-foot separation issue; pull the deed restrictions; and tell you whether an existing permit carries grandfathered nonconforming status. Those four things decide whether your pro forma is real, and all four are answerable before you spend a dollar on inspections.

Call or text 830-446-3847 · Email heath.shepard@kw.com

Heath Shepard, REALTOR — Keller Williams, Boerne and San Antonio. Eleven years in Texas real estate, with a background in land development. This page summarizes a city ordinance and is not legal advice — verify current requirements and fees directly with the City of Boerne.

title: Buying Land and Acreage in Kendall County, TX
metaTitle: Buying Land and Acreage in Kendall County, TX
metaDescription: Kendall County land: no zoning, no residential building code, wells, septic feasibility, ag valuation rollback and dark-sky permits. What to verify first.
summary: Kendall County has no zoning and no building code for single-family residential in unincorporated areas, so recorded deed restrictions are the only land-use control. Two items decide a land deal: septic feasibility, which needs a licensed site evaluator and a contract contingency, and well yield. Losing a 1-d-1 ag valuation triggers a rollback of back taxes.
body:
Kendall County is still, substantially, ranch country. The appraisal district's 2025 certified roll shows $1.98 billion in agricultural market value inside Boerne ISD alone, appraised at $9.2 million under productivity valuation — a productivity loss of $1.97 billion (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025 Certified Totals, as of Supplement 47, December 3, 2025). Roughly two-thirds of the taxable property accounts in Boerne ISD sit outside Boerne city limits.

Buying land here is a different transaction from buying a house. The failure modes are different, the diligence is different, and the cost of getting it wrong is larger — because unlike a house, land can turn out to be unbuildable.

The first thing to understand: nobody is protecting you

The Kendall County Engineer's office puts it plainly:

"Kendall County does not regulate land use and has not adopted zoning regulations in the unincorporated areas of the County."

"While Kendall County has not adopted building codes for single family residential developments, the County has adopted a Fire Code administered by the Kendall County Fire Marshal..."

(Kendall County Engineer, Permits Required, Building Codes, Certificates of Occupancy, and Zoning Regulations Verification Letter, March 4, 2026)

What the county does regulate: 911 addressing, subdivision of property, floodplain management, and permits for "placement or modification of driveways, any work within County-maintained right of way, outdoor lighting, on-site sewage facilities, and any site improvements whether within or outside of the floodplain." Development is defined broadly — "any man-made change to improved and unimproved real estate," including buildings, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavation, drilling, or storage of equipment or materials.

The Kendall County Health Department may also have requirements for certain multi-family and non-residential development. The Fire Marshal issues Certificates of Compliance and Certificates of Occupancy for certain multi-family and non-residential development.

The letter closes with the sentence that should govern your entire purchase: "The property owner must also abide by any subdivision conditions, covenants, restrictions and deed restrictions and home owners' association requirements in effect."

Translation: your deed restrictions are your zoning. If they don't prohibit it, your neighbor can do it. Read them completely, and read them for what they permit as much as what they forbid.

Septic feasibility: the question that decides the deal

On vacant land, this is the first thing to answer and the most common reason a land purchase falls apart.

Kendall County permits on-site sewage facilities and approves or denies an application within 30 days of receipt. Statewide rules live in TCEQ's 30 TAC Chapter 285, with county environmental health departments acting as Authorized Agents handling day-to-day permitting — and local programs can be more stringent than the state minimum.

What you need:

  • A licensed site evaluator to conduct a soil evaluation. Hill Country soil is frequently thin over limestone, and thin soil over rock drives you from a conventional system to an aerobic or other alternative system — a significant cost difference.
  • Confirmation of setbacks from wells, property lines, water features and easements.
  • A determination of what system type can be permitted, because that determines cost.
  • On steep terrain, confirmation that a drain field or spray area actually fits where the house needs to go.

Make the contract contingent on septic feasibility. A land contract with no septic contingency on an unevaluated tract is a gamble, not a purchase.

For an existing home, get the OSSF permit on file, the system design, the maintenance and pumping history, the maintenance contract status on an aerobic system, and a dedicated septic inspection. The general home inspector's look at a septic system is not a septic inspection.

Water: the other question that decides the deal

Kendall County sits inside the Hill Country Priority Groundwater Management Area — the region was declared a Critical Groundwater Area in 1990 — over the Trinity Aquifer. The Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District was created by county voters on November 5, 2002, to conserve, preserve, recharge, protect and prevent waste of groundwater in the county.

Texas law exempts most single-household domestic wells and many agricultural and livestock uses from permitting. Exempt is not the same as unregulated: districts can still require registration and spacing, and can set limits for permitted users during drought.

Your diligence list on an existing well:

  • Yield test, current, in writing. Not "the seller says it makes 15 gallons a minute."
  • Water quality test — bacteriological and chemical.
  • Registration status with Cow Creek GCD.
  • Well depth, casing depth and which formation it produces from. A shallow well in the upper Trinity behaves very differently in drought than a deeper one.
  • Pump age and service history.
  • Drought performance. Ask neighbors. This is the one question where local memory beats any document.
  • If it's a shared well, read the shared-well agreement line by line: who pays for the pump, who controls access, what happens when the other party won't pay, and what the remedy is.

On raw land with no well, get a drilling quote and talk to a local driller about what depth and yield is typical on that specific side of the county. It is not uniform.

Also confirm whether the tract is within a water supply corporation or Kendall County WCID #1 service area — WCID #1 carries its own tax rate of 0.166106 (Kendall Appraisal District, 2025), and service availability and connection fees are their own investigation.

Agricultural valuation: worth real money, and easy to lose

A 1-d-1 open-space agricultural valuation is the difference between paying tax on market value and paying tax on productivity value. In Boerne ISD, ag land carried $1.98 billion in market value and $9.2 million in productivity value in 2025. That is the scale of what's at stake.

From the Kendall County Ag Use Manual, the district's own published guidelines:

History requirement: the land must have been used principally for agriculture or timber production for five of the preceding seven years.

Degree of intensity, by enterprise:

Enterprise Kendall County minimum
Cow/calf Minimum 3 calves and 10 acres
Sheep Ewes plus 1 ram on 10 acres
Goats 6 does and 1 buck, minimum 10 acres
Exotics Minimum 10 acres, wire mesh fencing
Beekeeping Not less than 5 nor more than 20 acres; minimum 6 hives
Orchard / vineyard Minimum 3 acres
Market garden Minimum 3 acres — family gardens do not qualify
Wildlife management Minimum of three approved practices

Stocking rates by range type:

Range type Carrying capacity
Improved Grass Range 1 animal unit per 5 acres
Native Range I 1 AU per 10 acres
Native Range II 1 AU per 25 acres
Native Range III (oak) 1 AU per 35 acres
Native Range III (cedar) 1 AU per 50 acres

An animal unit is a 1,000-pound cow.

Those cedar and oak numbers are the practitioner detail buyers miss. A 40-acre cedar-covered tract at 1 AU per 50 acres does not carry enough capacity to meet a cow/calf degree-of-intensity standard on its own. Acreage alone does not qualify you. Range condition does.

The rollback

If you buy land under an ag valuation and stop the qualifying use, you can trigger a rollback of back taxes. On a tract carrying a productivity valuation that's a fraction of market value, that liability can be substantial.

Decide before you close:

  • Are you continuing the existing use? Then get the lease, the livestock arrangement or the wildlife plan documented and in place at closing — not "sometime after we move in."
  • Are you converting to residential? Then price the rollback into your offer and know the number before you sign.
  • Wildlife management is the common path for buyers who want the valuation without running livestock. It requires the land to already qualify under 1-d-1 and a Texas Parks & Wildlife-compliant plan implementing a minimum of three approved practices. Get a wildlife biologist involved before closing, not after the first tax notice.

Access, easements and the survey

Order a new survey. An old one that predates a fence line, a pond, an outbuilding or a neighbor's improvement will cost you far more in a boundary dispute than the survey saved.

What the survey and the title commitment's Schedule B need to establish:

  • Legal access, not just a gravel road that has always been there. A tract with only historical access and no recorded easement is a real problem.
  • Easement locations — pipeline, electric, water, drainage. A pipeline easement through the middle of your building site is the most expensive thing you can discover after closing.
  • Encroachments in either direction.
  • Floodplain boundaries relative to the building site.
  • Mineral and surface rights. In Texas these sever, and in a county with any oil, gas or aggregate interest the surface owner can end up with an operator's surface rights they didn't expect. Ask what conveys.

Floodplain and drainage

Kendall County administers floodplain management and requires permits for site improvements whether inside or outside the floodplain. Cibolo Creek and its tributaries have flooded the Boerne area repeatedly, and flood zone designation varies parcel by parcel — sometimes within the same subdivision.

Pull the FEMA FIRM panel for the exact parcel. Then go further, because FEMA maps do not capture every risk in Central Texas:

  • Walk the property and find the drainage. Where does water go in a hard rain?
  • Where is the low-water crossing between the building site and the paved road? A property that's dry but unreachable eight times a year is a real problem that no flood map shows you.
  • Ask about the 2013 and earlier events specifically. People here remember.

Dark sky lighting

Kendall County requires a permit prior to the installation of any outdoor lights, and regulated outdoor lighting must use International Dark-Sky Association compliant products installed per manufacturer or IDA specifications. The county adopted a night sky resolution in January 2020 and has pursued International Dark Sky Community designation. The City of Boerne has its own dark-sky regulations in its Unified Development Code.

If you're planning an arena, a lit sport court, security lighting on a shop or extensive landscape lighting, check the requirements before you design and budget. This is one of the genuinely good things about living here — the night sky in Kendall County is worth protecting — but it is a permit, not a suggestion.

Utilities and infrastructure cost

Outside city limits there are no city utilities. Electric service comes from a cooperative — Bandera Electric Cooperative and Pedernales Electric Cooperative both serve portions of Kendall County, and the City of Boerne's own PUC-defined electric service area extends somewhat beyond the city limits, so verify who serves the specific parcel.

Budget lines people forget on raw land:

  • Electric service extension to a remote building site. This can be a five-figure number and it is quoted by the cooperative, not estimated by your builder.
  • Driveway and culvert — permitted by the county.
  • Propane tank and initial fill.
  • Well drilling, casing, pump, pressure tank, and a line to the house.
  • Septic system, sized to the house.
  • Fencing, which on acreage is expensive and is frequently in worse shape than it looks from the road.
  • Brush management, particularly cedar, which is ongoing rather than one-time.

Taxes on land

Combined 2025 rates for unincorporated Kendall County (Kendall Appraisal District):

Stack Rate
Kendall County + Boerne ISD + Cow Creek 1.3929
Kendall County + Comfort ISD + Cow Creek 1.3148
Add Kendall County MUD #1 2.0429
Add Miralomas MUD 2.3929
Comfort ISD + Kendall County WCID #1 + Cow Creek 1.480906

Note that neither the City of Boerne nor Kendall County offers a general residence homestead exemption — your only general homestead exemption is the $140,000 school district amount. On land you're holding without a residence, you have no homestead exemption at all, which is exactly why the ag valuation matters so much here.

Looking at a tract in Kendall County? Send me the parcel and I'll pull the appraisal district record, tell you whether it carries an ag valuation and what a rollback would look like, confirm the school district and combined tax rate, check the FEMA panel, and flag the access and easement questions from the title work. My background before real estate was land development, and land is the part of this market where a bad assumption costs the most.
